sources.entry: Elengrab - Fast cross-platform video and audio downloader and media viewer with flexible format and quality options. Supports 1000+ websites including YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitch and more. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Elengrab is a self-hosted, Go-based web app for downloading video and audio from 1,000+ sites via yt-dlp and watching them in a browser with a YouTube-like interface.
summary.what_it_does: Elengrab downloads video and audio from more than 1,000 websites using yt-dlp extractors, with configurable format and quality settings. It runs a task queue with concurrent workers, and tasks can be added or removed instantly. Downloaded media is browsable in a web UI with thumbnails, previews, search, sorting, grid and list views, short share links, and resume-playback tracking. The frontend uses plain HTML, CSS, HTMX and vanilla JavaScript, and the app ships as a single binary or a Docker image. The README also describes access modes (public, public read-only, guest session-isolated, and authenticated), optional cookie support for sites such as YouTube, and mobile sharing from other apps.
use_cases: download YouTube videos to a home server
save Instagram, TikTok or Twitch videos
share downloaded media via short links
access a private media service remotely
how_to_run: Standalone: download the latest release binary for your OS from GitHub Releases
Open the web interface on port 8080 in a browser
Optional: docker-compose up -d using the README's compose file
notable: Covers 1,000+ sites through yt-dlp extractors, including YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Twitch
Mobile sharing: videos shared from apps like YouTube are picked up and downloaded automatically
Multiple access modes, from anonymous public use to login-required authenticated mode
PWA support, so it can be installed as a standalone app
Single binary for Windows, Linux and macOS, or a lightweight Docker container
caveats: Requires yt-dlp and ffmpeg installed separately in standalone mode; Deno is needed for cookie support
Resource-heavy during downloading, merging and transcoding; about 512 MB RAM minimum and 4 GB recommended
Users are responsible for complying with copyright and platform terms of service
